headline: 2 held as youths trafficked to Cambodia for online scams
summary: Victims were lured with job promises, sold for $5,000, and forced into fraudulent activities after their passports were seized.
details: The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of police has arrested two members of a human trafficking ring in Dhaka’s Paltan area on Tuesday.

caption:
Lured by job promises, two youths were sold for $5,000 each to a Cambodian scam centre.

The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of police has arrested two members of a human trafficking ring in Dhaka’s Paltan area on Tuesday.

The suspects are accused of luring two Bangladeshi youths to Cambodia with promises of lucrative employment, only to sell them to a 'scam centre'.

According to the CID, the victims' passports were confiscated upon arrival and they were sold for $5,000 each.

The victims were held captive and subjected to physical and mental abuse to force them to engage in fraudulent online activities.

The trafficking ring had collected approximately Tk 600,000 from each of the victims' families for the travel arrangements.

Traffickers later demanded an additional $5,000 for their release, which the families paid, along with further funds for return tickets.

The victims managed to contact the BRAC Migration Centre, which facilitated their return to Bangladesh on September 3.

The two victims filed a case at the Paltan Police Station on Monday, which led to the the arrests.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, bdnews24.com, Prothom Alo
